state.context: We are implementing Can HTTP internals with no backwards-compatibility burden. The specified response is opaque and immutable; each named callback must finish before the adapter converts it exactly once using native Response. Can does not prescribe linear ownership for a response, but native response streams are consumable. Paths for exact GET/POST dispatch use URL normalization followed by decodeURIComponent; HEAD has no automatic GET alias, and neither captures nor wildcards exist. Normalization can merge different source spellings. The available route errors are duplicate_route(method,path) and ambiguous_route(first,second). Public operation signatures remain fixed; only implementation representation and collision treatment are being selected.

response.instructions: Assess which response lifetime model follows the given Can value and native sink semantics.

criteria.snapshot: Retain a hidden frozen response description and materialize it into a distinct native Response exactly once at each request boundary, including when handlers reuse a Can value.
criteria.consume: Give the response token one conversion lifetime, invalidating it for all later callback results.
criteria.cache: Materialize the native Response only once over the value lifetime, then send the identical native instance for subsequent callbacks.

routes.instructions: Determine the strongest fit for alias and duplicate detection under the supplied exact-routing rules.

criteria.collision: Apply identical native normalization to requests and valid static declarations, classify same-method identical declarations as duplicate_route and same-method alias collisions as ambiguous_route, and permit both GET and POST at one destination.
criteria.strict: Forbid all noncanonical spellings through invalid_route at route construction, so normalized aliases never participate in router collision analysis.
criteria.overwrite: Select the final registration whenever normalization maps several route declarations to one method and path.
